items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: She hadn't learned the verse to Gershwin’s “Let’s Call the Whole Thing Off.”

ctx.x: When you get a commission do you prefer that you be wide open to decide what to do or do you prefer some guidance? I mean what kind of guidance comes with a commission?

Yeah I love both. I love being complet – in this instance there were no parameters given except, “We want you and Marvin to come and be the soloists. You pick the material, you title the production.” So that was completely wide open. I chose tunes that were related to “52nd Street Theme,” “Broadway Boogie” by Ornette Coleman, “All Across the City” Jim Hall, “There’s a Boat Leaving Soon for New York” etcetera, etcetera, and I wrote an original called “Manhattan Soliloquy.” But then there are projects like, well…

verse trying to teach it to her and she says, “Well you sound great, you sing it.” And I said, “What are you talking about, it’s your date?” She said, “Roll the tape, you sing it.” So I did and I ended up on the record, I think it was the first time I’d ever sung on anybody’s album. And then that opened a Pandora’s box, you can’t shut me up. I love to sing and I’ve sung on several of my recordings since. For better or for worse.
